newsitem.title: USA: Lynch sees uncertainty in value of licenses.
newsitem.headline: Lynch sees uncertainty in value of licenses.

text.p: Lynch Corp said Monday it was uncertain if the Federal Communications Commission would give Fortunet Communications LP relief for interest, principal payments and ownership restrictions on its licenses to provide personal communications services.

Lynch, which owns 49.9 percent of Fortunet, said the FCC's decisions would affect Fortunet's ability to obtain vendor and third-party financing and its ability to enter operating agreements for its licenses.
"The future realizability of our investment in these licenses will be based on the decisions of the FCC," Lynch said in a statement.

The company also said that it based its personal communications services legal, financial and operating models and structure in part on its ability to amortize certain costs for tax purposes. "Subsequent events proved this approach faulty," the company statement said.
The company did not elaborate, and corporate Secretary Robert Hurwich also declined to elaborate.
Lynch also said that the value of other licenses to provide personal communications services may be below what was paid.
Those licenses were acquired by Aer Force Communications, which is also 49.9 percent owned by Lynch.
Lynch said Aer Force acquired these licenses at a cost of $19 million, of which the Government financed $15.2 million.
